headline: Indonesia's Free School Health Program Reaches 8.8 Million Students
meta_description: Over 8.8 million Indonesian students have been screened through a nationwide free health check program covering nearly 303,000 schools.
summary_short: A nationwide free school health screening program in Indonesia has now reached 8.8 million students across nearly 303,000 schools, catching health problems early.
body:
Over 8.8 million Indonesian students have been screened through a nationwide free school health check program, with the initiative now covering nearly 303,000 schools across the country.

The program represents a significant public health effort, providing early detection and intervention for health issues among the student population. By making these screenings free and accessible in schools themselves, the initiative removes barriers that might otherwise prevent vulnerable young people from receiving needed medical attention.

Early health screening in schools is particularly valuable for catching conditions that might otherwise go unnoticed, especially in communities with limited access to healthcare services. With such a large reach across Indonesian schools, the program demonstrates the scale at which preventive health care can be delivered when integrated into existing educational infrastructure.
quick_facts: 8.8 million Indonesian students screened so far
Free health checks provided to all participants
Early detection of health problems emphasized
